MANDARIN — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #11
====

GRADE: Grade 9
SUBJECT: MANDARIN
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KJSEA

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. In MANDARIN, the best classroom habit is: (1 mark)
   A. Mix random languages with no purpose
   B. Avoid speaking to classmates
   C. Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day
   D. Only memorise without using the language

2. When practising Active Listening, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Active Listening.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Active Listening.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Active Listening.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.

3. When practising Oral Expression, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Oral Expression.
   B. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Oral Expression.
   D. Use insults to “practise” Oral Expression.

4. When practising Interactive Speaking, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Interactive Speaking.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Interactive Speaking.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Interactive Speaking.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

5. When practising Reading for Information, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Reading for Information.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading for Information.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading for Information.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.

6. When practising Phonological Awareness, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Phonological Awareness.
   B. Copy random text without understanding Phonological Awareness.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Phonological Awareness.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness.

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
7. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Information and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

8. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Fluency and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

9. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Understanding and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

10. In three clear sentences, explain Reading for Comprehension and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
pages.answers:
MARKING SCHEME
====

1. C — Practise listening, speaking, reading, and writing every day

2. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Active Listening.

3. B — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Oral Expression.

4. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Interactive Speaking.

5. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading for Information.

6. D — Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Phonological Awareness.

7. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading for Information; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

8. (4 marks)

9. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading for Understanding; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.

10. (4 marks)
Award marks for: (1) accurate definition/idea of Reading for Comprehension; (2) correct use of subject terms; (3) a relevant local example (home, school, market, farm, or community). Do not award for slogans with no content.
